title: Jaime King Addresses Absence from Taylor Swift's Wedding and the Status of Their Friendship
text:
Jaime King's publicist explains why she and Swift's godson Leo Thames were not at the singer's wedding. The statement highlights the private nature of their bond amid reports of a strained friendship following King's custody battle.
Taylor Swift 's former best friend Jaime King has addressed their current relationship following the absence of both King and Swift's godson from the pop star's recent wedding to Travis Kelce .
The 47-year-old actress, known for her roles in White Chicks and Hart of Dixie, has a long history with Swift. A key connection is that Swift became the godmother to King's son Leo Thames in 2015. The couple's friendship, which was once very public, appeared to strain last year after King lost custody of her two sons, Leo and James, following a protracted legal battle with her ex-husband Kyle Newman.
Swift and Kelce were married in a lavish ceremony at Madison Square Garden in New York City last week, attended by around 1,000 guests. Among them were Kelce's brother Jason and his daughters, who served as flower girls. Notably absent, however, were Swift's five godchildren, including Leo Thames and the four children of her friend Blake Lively. In a statement provided to Page Six by her publicist Jane Owen, King explained the absence.
The statement clarified that Leo, who is now ten years old, is 'still too young for a large adult wedding celebration.
' It was noted that King and Leo were able to celebrate the marriage 'in his own very special, age-appropriate way during his summer break. ' The publicist emphasized the personal nature of the godmother role, stating, 'The reason Jaime chose Taylor as Leo Thames's godmother is because they both believe that being a godmother is a deeply personal and spiritual commitment that has nothing to do with public appearances.
' This perspective suggests the bond between Swift and Leo exists outside the realm of social events and media scrutiny. The history between Swift and King is significant. Their friendship blossomed in the 2010s. In 2014, King's then-husband Kyle Newman directed the music video for Swift's hit 'Style' from her 1989 album.
The following year, Swift officially became godmother to Leo. At the time, King praised Swift effusively in an interview with E! News, saying, 'I always thought if I were to have another child that she would be the ideal godmother because the way she not only treats me but the way she treats other human beings. She's so loving and so giving and so generous and she does everything from her heart and she's incredibly brave and authentic.
It's a very rare thing to come across.
' She added, 'I know that he will always have a very good person and role model through her. ' The shift in their relationship became public knowledge in March of the previous year when King lost physical custody of her sons. A source told The U.S. Sun that while Swift and King no longer have 'regular contact,' 'there is still love.
' The insider stated, 'Taylor and Jaime are not close anymore and don't talk but there is still love. ' Despite the distance, it was reported that Swift remains committed to her godmotherly duties and would 'be there in a heartbeat' for Leo if needed. King's custody battle with Newman was lengthy and contentious.
The judge in the case granted Newman sole physical custody and ordered that King's visits with her sons must be supervised until she completes a court-mandated drug and alcohol program for approximately six months. This personal turmoil coincided with the cooling of her friendship with Swift. More recently, King's personal life has seen further upheaval. She married business investor Austin Sosa in July 2025 after a brief engagement.
However, in January, it was revealed that Sosa had filed for divorce, leaving King reportedly 'blindsided.
' Through all these changes, the narrative around Swift's role as godmother, as framed by King's publicist, underscores a private, enduring promise that transcends public ceremonies and evolving personal circumstances
